summary: Republic of Korea Economic Summation No. 35 covers September and October 1948, the first economic report after USAMGIK handed authority to the Republic of Korea, and continues the SKIG Activities series. It records transfer of American-run departments to Korean ministries and the end of the Office of Property Custody under US control on 12 October. Main topics are the grain collection programs, ration-roll inflation, falling electric power, coal imports, prices, trade, currency growth and finances. Part I covers refugees and vested property sales; Part II food, prices, industry, mining, allocations and trade; Part III transport, communications, utilities and public works; Part IV finance. Historians will find provincial quotas, ration estimates, trade statistics, power figures, and the barter suspension with North Korea, in statistical tables.
highlights: Summer grain collection reached 107,766 metric tons, 100.4 percent of quota (Cheju only 4 percent), and the 1948 rice collection goal was set at 1,125,000 tons, split by province.
Ration rolls listed 9,987,597 persons in October, up nearly 1,000,000 in a year; officials suspected a 'ghost population', about 500,000 of it in Seoul.
The Office of Property Custody passed to a Korean custodian on 12 October, with 1,279 cumulative sales worth about 2,611 million won; immovable sales halted 18 September.
Electricity deliveries fell about 18 percent below August, to 45.6 million KWH in September; Yongwol's rehabilitated plant carried 80,400 KW in a 23 October test.
Currency in circulation rose 2,500 million won from 31 August to 31 October, over 1,500 million of it for Monopoly tobacco purchases; the overdraft reached 38,400 million won.
Bituminous coal imports from Japan reached 100,015 metric tons in September, 73 percent above the 1947 monthly average, while anthracite output fell a fifth month, 51 percent below April.
Commerce Minister Louise Yim suspended barter trade with North Korea pending Assembly approval; it resumed by end of October under modified rules, mainly manufactured goods.
Wholesale prices fell to 177 percent of the 1947 average in October from 184 in August, and September exports were 45 percent of imports, with Hong Kong taking over 93 percent.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover, blank digitization pages, foreword and contents of Economic Summation No. 35 (September-October 1948), the first under the Republic, successor to SKIG Activities; No. 36 is planned through December.

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Agencies shifted to Korean management. Summer grain collection reached 107,766 tons (100.4 percent of goal), a 1,125,000-ton rice goal was set, and ration rolls were suspected padded. Electricity fell 18 percent; currency rose 2,500 million won.

sections.title: Part I. Basic Aspects
sections.summary: Refugee arrivals across the 38th parallel and the 12 October transfer of the Office of Property Custody, with 1,279 cumulative vested-property sales.

sections.title: Section 1. Population
sections.summary: Refugee entries across the 38th parallel were 11,718 in September and 7,764 in October (1948 total 106,463). Net movement since October 1945 added 1,588,030 residents.

sections.title: Refugee Migration
sections.summary: Refugee entries were 11,718 in September (up 57 percent on August) and 7,764 in October (down 33 percent), attributed to colder weather. January-October totals fell 34 percent in 1948 against 1947.

sections.title: Population Movement
sections.summary: From 1 October 1945 to 31 October 1948, 887,301 left South Korea (705,056 Japanese civilians) and 2,475,331 entered, including 1,117,819 Koreans from Japan and 646,034 from North Korea; net gain 1,588,030.

sections.title: Section 2. Vested Property
sections.summary: Office of Property Custody passed to a Korean custodian on 12 October 1948, with 1,279 cumulative sales worth about 2,611 million won. Immovable sales halted 18 September; KRMC planned low-cost housing.

sections.title: Administration Division
sections.summary: Office of Property Custody shrank before transfer: American staff fell from 96 to 58, and Korean employees from 2,948 to 2,635 (national office 468, provincial offices 2,167).

sections.title: Property Disposal
sections.summary: 581 sales worth 1,358.4 million won since 1 July brought the total to 1,279. Sales of immovables and shares stopped 18 September under the financial agreement; OPC asked to ship 1,600 tons of steel billets to the US.

sections.title: Korean Residence Management Corporation
sections.summary: KRMC planned 500 low-cost houses (types B, C, D) costing about 240 million won, financed by subsidy, loans, lot sales and 20 percent down payments. Police guarded 149,056 pyung of lots.

sections.title: Real Estate Transfers
sections.summary: The department accepted US-released property, with Korean agencies given priority under Procedural Memorandums 21 and 24: 280 dependent houses and 625 other properties. The 30 September quarterly rent could not be paid.

sections.title: Policy Division
sections.summary: Of 1,394 cases from the Property Claims Commission, 825 were allowed, 356 disallowed and 213 returned. Ordinance No. 210 claim forms went out 24 August; the Custodian held shares in 38 corporations.

sections.title: Comptroller Division
sections.summary: Manuals on taxes, loans and auditing were translated to train Korean staff. Korean auditors, supervised by an American, made quarterly audits of all provincial offices and of custodian-controlled firms.

sections.title: Part II. Production and Supply
sections.summary: Food, prices, industry, mining, allocations and trade: summer grain at 100.4 percent of quota, wholesale prices down to 177, bituminous imports of 100,015 tons, 1,211 allocations, and exports at 45 percent of imports.

sections.title: Section 1. Food and Agriculture
sections.summary: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry took over 13 September. Summer grain reached 107,766 tons; the rice quota was 1,125,000 tons. Ration rolls were inflated; fertilizer imports, forestry and land payments reported.

sections.title: Administrative Changes and Rice Collection
sections.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry took over food agencies on 13 September and the National Land Administration on 11 October. A 1,125,000-ton rice quota was split by province; summer grain hit 100.4 percent, Cheju 4.

sections.title: Food
sections.summary: Ration rolls rose to 9,987,597 in October, with padding suspected; grain was released to 9,285,000 recipients. Stocks fell to 170,551 tons. Imports included 18,328 tons of milo maize.

sections.title: Korea Agricultural Association
sections.summary: Fertilizer imports from October 1946 to October 1948 totaled 630,777 tons. Of 521,776 tons received by provinces since July 1947, 461,344 (88 percent) were sold to farmers; 7,878 were apparent losses.

sections.title: Bureau of Forestry
sections.summary: September and October output: plywood 10,000 and 12,000 pieces; logs 19,700 and 21,300 cubic meters; fuelwood 313,889 and 293,714; charcoal 3,660 and 3,960 tons. Fuelwood alone fell in October.

sections.title: National Land Administration
sections.summary: Land purchasers pay 20 percent of annual crop output for 15 years. October installments were 10,801 tons (70.5 percent of 15,315 due), only 24.4 percent at Iri; rents 477 tons (58.8 percent).

sections.title: Section 2. Prices
sections.summary: Wholesale index fell to 177 percent of the 1947 average in October from 184 in August as grains declined after floods eased; cotton cloth and firewood rose. Retail prices followed.

sections.title: Wholesale Prices
sections.summary: Wholesale indexes fell in October to 177 percent of the 1947 average (184 in August) on lower grains and protein foods. Cotton sheeting and sookso silk rose on power cuts; firewood jumped seasonally.

sections.title: Retail Prices
sections.summary: Seoul retail prices and nine-city indexes followed wholesale prices. Cleaned rice fell from 2,480 won per mal in September to 1,800; firewood and kimchi vegetables rose. Table 6 put the October retail index at 175.

sections.title: Controlled Prices
sections.summary: Controlled prices were set by the former National Price Administration, now the Bureau of Prices in the Office of Planning. No new prices were set after the Republic took over; cleaned rice was 300 won per large mal.

sections.title: Section 3. Industrial Production
sections.summary: Output improved slightly despite the power shortage. Flour, noodles, coal briquettes (15,849 tons in October), insulators and oxygen set 1948 highs. Cement stopped in early November for lack of power; no carbide was made.

sections.title: Section 4. Mining and Minerals
sections.summary: Anthracite output fell for a fifth month, 51 percent below April. Lignite rose to 5,496 tons, bituminous imports from Japan reached 100,015 tons in September, and gold, silver, copper, tungsten and graphite recovered.

sections.title: Indigenous Anthracite and Lignite Coal
sections.summary: Anthracite output fell a fifth month, 51 percent below April, from power shortage. Lignite reached 5,496 tons; the 70,500-ton quota proved unrealistic, Samchuk made 21,650 tons, and Yongwol 19,636 short tons in October.

sections.title: Bituminous Coal and Shipments to Consumers
sections.summary: Bituminous imports from Japan were 100,015 tons in September, 73 percent above the 1947 monthly average, and 90,297 tons in October. September supply was 18,474 tons of anthracite and 64,566 of bituminous.

sections.title: Other Minerals
sections.summary: Non-coal minerals recovered in September: gold 15.9 kg, silver 129.6 kg, copper concentrate 276 tons, tungsten ore 119.4 tons. Zinc (31.8 tons) and lead (33.8) resumed after flood stoppage.

sections.title: Section 5. Allocations and Distribution
sections.summary: Allocations Bureau processed 1,211 allocations worth 2,551.8 million won; 37,181 tons of salt distributed; petroleum deliveries fell short of allocations. Barter trade with North Korea was suspended, then resumed under restrictions.

sections.title: Allocation of Consumer Goods
sections.summary: The Allocations Bureau replaced the National Consumer Goods Office on 16 August and had processed 1,211 allocations worth 2,551.8 million won by October, farmers receiving 37 percent. September-October allocations: 116, worth 367.4 million won.

sections.title: Distribution of Controlled Commodities
sections.summary: Federation of Financial Associations purchases of controlled goods totaled 315.95 million won in September and 117.75 million in October, mainly cotton cloth and underwear, against 3,577.8 million since July 1946.

sections.title: Salt Distribution
sections.summary: 37,181 tons of salt were distributed in September and October, mostly kimchi rations. Stock on 31 October was 89,927 tons; government salterns made 88,637 tons since April, 66 percent of the F/Y 1948/49 estimate.

sections.title: Petroleum
sections.summary: Petroleum deliveries fell short of allocations, such as 6.48 million liters of gasoline in October against 7.78 million allocated, owing to stock shortages and poor Pusan terminal facilities. Korean use fell from 409 million liters in 1937 to 48 million in 1944.

sections.title: Barter Trade with North Korea
sections.summary: Minister Louise Yim ordered trade with North Korea suspended pending National Assembly approval and barred exports of food, rubber, cotton cloth and petroleum. By end of October the Assembly approved and barter resumed under modified rules.

sections.title: Section 6. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Private imports rose 22 percent and exports 80 percent in September, exports reaching 45 percent of imports. Government shipments went to the US, Hong Kong and Japan; souvenirs were sold to Americans.

sections.title: Private Trade Statistics
sections.summary: September imports were 1,155 million won (newsprint, raw rubber, thread, plate glass); exports 516 million (shellfish, agar), 93 percent to Hong Kong. Imports rose 22 percent and exports over 80 percent; Inchon handled 96 percent of imports.

sections.title: Government-to-Government Transactions
sections.summary: October government shipments to the US exceeded 3,600 tons, mostly 3,595.6 tons of scrap metal ($106,941). Over 5,800 tons went to Japan from 15 August, chiefly 4,108 tons of graphite.

sections.title: Korean Items for Americans in Korea
sections.summary: Korean-made souvenirs such as brassware and lacquer sold at the Seoul Army PX: 10,414 pieces ($11,274) in August, 4,850 ($5,399) in September, 5,320 ($4,259) in October.

sections.title: Part III. Public Services
sections.summary: Railroads, communications, utilities and public works: transport and communications departments passed to Korean ministries, power deliveries fell 18 percent, and Public Works became a bureau under Home Affairs.

sections.title: Section 1. Transportation
sections.summary: Transportation department turned over 15 August. September expenditures rose 61 percent to a postliberation high of 1,418.6 million won; passengers and freight rose, operable locomotives fell to 256, and coal use increased.

sections.title: Railroads
sections.summary: Transportation passed to the Republic on 15 August; Min He-sik resigned 6 October, succeeded by Ho Chung. September spending peaked at 1,418.6 million won. Operable locomotives fell to 256; employment declined while wages rose.

sections.title: Marine, Highway and Air Transportation
sections.summary: Railroad coal use rose to 45,919 tons in September and 49,923 in October. Marine income rose to 28.6 and 32.4 million won; September marine spending spiked to 206 million won, then fell to 28 million.

sections.title: Section 2. Communications
sections.summary: Communications passed to the Republic on 13 September under Minister Yoon Suk-ku. September revenue nearly doubled on higher telephone rates; expenditure hit 201 million won with 12,570 employees. Seoul-Shanghai radio-telephone tests began.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Utilities
sections.summary: Power deliveries were 45.6 million KWH in September and 46.1 million in October, about 18 percent below August. Yongwol's rehabilitated plant carried 80,400 KW on 23 October; a seven-man power mission under Loyal R. Millburn arrived 19 October.

sections.title: Section 4. Public Works
sections.summary: Public Works became a Home Affairs bureau on 13 September. Highway projects used 82,677 man-days and 41.3 million won; Waegwon bridge finished. Water plants were repaired and river works planned at 82.4 million won.

sections.title: Part IV. Finance
sections.summary: Government finance and non-government finance: notes outstanding rose 2,500 million won, the overdraft reached 38,400 million, and deposits stood at 52,328 million won at end of September.

sections.title: Section 1. Government Finance
sections.summary: Notes outstanding rose 2,500 million won from August to October, over 1,500 million for tobacco purchases. Spending exceeded revenue by 3,695 million in September and 878 million in October; appropriations reached 43,749 million won.

sections.title: Section 2. Non-Government Finance
sections.summary: Deposits reached 52,328 million won at end of September (38 percent government, 51 public); Bank of Chosun held nearly 36 percent. Loans outstanding fell 960 million to 27,441 million won.

sections.title: Back matter
sections.summary: Blank pages marked 'Digitized by Google', a library due-date slip and a closing page; no report content.
